title: Battery handling and charging safety
introduction:
I make battery preparation part of the job before a tool reaches a terminal: arrange ventilation and eye protection, keep ignition sources away, and plan how the battery will be lifted and its venting restored.

The sulfuric-acid precautions and the separate Li-ion precautions address different battery hazards. Identify the battery technology and apply the relevant instructions. This is a safety reference; charger selection, charging settings, connection order and battery removal require the matching service instructions.

items.name: Work area and eye protection
items.detail: Provide a well-ventilated area, shield the eyes against acid splashes, and keep flames, sparks and burning substances away from the battery.

items.name: Lifting equipment
items.detail: For a plastic-cased battery, use a battery carrier or support opposite corners by hand.

items.name: Li-ion tools and personal items
items.detail: When working with a Li-ion Battery, use insulated tools only, remove metallic personal items, and keep objects off the battery.

edits.text: WARNING: Batteries contain sulfuric acid and produce explosive gases. Work in a well-ventilated area, and keep the battery away from flames, sparks and burning substances. Avoid acid contact with skin, eyes and clothing. Shield your eyes whenever working near the battery to protect against acid splashes. If acid contacts skin or eyes, immediately flush with water for a minimum of 15 minutes, then obtain prompt medical attention. If acid is swallowed, call a physician immediately. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Ventilation and ignition-source control address explosive gases; eye protection and immediate flushing address acid exposure.

edits.text: WARNING: Always lift a plastic-cased battery with a battery carrier or with your hands on opposite corners. Excessive pressure on the end walls can force acid through the vent caps, causing personal injury and/or damage to the vehicle or battery.
edits.why: The prescribed support avoids squeezing the case end walls during lifting.

edits.text: WARNING: Whenever the battery vent tube has been disconnected, always reconnect it properly to the battery. An incorrectly restored vent connection can allow harmful gases into the vehicle’s cabin, causing serious personal injury or death.
edits.why: Restoring the vent connection is a required completion step after it has been disturbed.

edits.text: WARNING: Battery posts, terminals and related accessories contain lead and lead components. Wash your hands after handling them. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Hand washing is required after contact with these battery components.
The following warnings specifically address Li-ion Batteries.

edits.text: WARNING: Explosion and fire hazard. Li-ion Battery terminals are always live. Never place items or tools on the Li-ion Battery. Avoid short circuits and excessive discharge/charge rates. Use insulated tools only, and do not wear metallic items such as watches, bracelets or rings. Failure to follow these instructions may result in a fire or serious personal injury.
edits.why: Treating the terminals as live governs tool choice, personal items and what may be placed near them.

edits.text: WARNING: Never attempt to open or disassemble the Li-ion Battery. Its electrolyte is very corrosive, although contact is not possible under normal working conditions. If the case is damaged, do not touch exposed electrolyte or powder. Failure to follow these instructions may result in serious personal injury.
edits.why: Case damage changes the exposure hazard; it does not authorize opening the battery.
